ltv_assumptions: ARPU is the primary MSP tier at $199/month, before per-device overage. Blended ARPU in a mature cohort would reach roughly $230 as client counts grow, but overage is excluded here because no cohort exists to estimate expansion from
Lifespan derived from retention.json base-case monthly churn of 6%, giving 1/0.06 = 16.7 months
estimated_ltv is the base-case contribution LTV (gross LTV x gross margin), which is the figure used for every ratio in this file
Confidence is medium rather than high: pricing is modelled rather than tested, and churn is benchmarked from the SMB self-serve band because the category publishes no retention data

gross_margin_note: Telemetry ingestion, per-tenant storage, browser-extension infrastructure and document generation are modest. Support is the dominant variable cost and is heavier than typical for this price point, because compliance-adjacent products draw questions the buyer is afraid to get wrong and because the MSP is fielding its own client's questions through the vendor. 82% rather than the 88-90% a pure software product would carry.

optimistic.condition: Rebilling is adopted by most customers, signup is qualified on client count, and no MSP-platform incumbent ships a competing module within the first two years.

pessimistic.condition: MSPs buy without packaging the service commercially, so the tool stays a cost line, and Purview coverage improves enough that clients question the separate invoice at first renewal.

founder_budget_tier_note: budget_constraint is 'low' at under $100/month, captured from the founder on 2026-09-06. Bootstrap tier: paid acquisition is off the table entirely, not merely constrained. Every paid channel below is marked skipped rather than modelled, per the channel relevance filter.

cac_by_channel_b2b.channel: MSP peer groups and operator communities (r/msp, MSP Slack and Discord groups, local peer groups)
cac_by_channel_b2b.cac_basis: Time cost of sustained community participation, amortised over conversions. Assumes roughly 4 hours a week of genuine participation producing a customer every six to eight weeks once established.
cac_by_channel_b2b.scale_ceiling: LOW. Realistically 10-25 customers over 18 months. r/msp and most MSP communities are explicitly hostile to vendor self-promotion and ban for it, so participation must be genuine and slow. The ceiling is set by how many people one founder can build credibility with, not by market size.

cac_by_channel_b2b.channel: Content and comparison SEO aimed at MSPs
cac_by_channel_b2b.cac_basis: Content production time at 15 hours a week amortised over conversions at a 12% trial-to-paid rate. Priced well above the $200-600 B2B band because the SERP is contested: Torii, Netwrix, MintMCP, Rhindon Cyber, ShadowLock and Lavawall are all publishing comparison content for these exact queries, several with funded content teams.
cac_by_channel_b2b.scale_ceiling: MEDIUM, and slow. This is the only channel with a ceiling above a few dozen customers, but it needs 6-12 months to ramp at 15 hours a week against competitors already ranking. It fails the 3:1 bar entirely in the pessimistic churn case.

cac_by_channel_b2b.channel: Outbound email and LinkedIn direct messages to MSP owners
cac_by_channel_b2b.cac_basis: Time cost of list building, sequencing and follow-up. MSP owners are identifiable by title and firmographics, which is the one thing working in this channel's favour.
cac_by_channel_b2b.scale_ceiling: LOW-MEDIUM. MSPs are among the most heavily prospected buyers in software and filter aggressively. A vendor with no SOC 2 attestation, no reviews and no partner programme is exactly what their filters are built to remove.

cac_by_channel_b2b.channel: Partner programme and integration listings (RMM and PSA marketplaces, MSP tool directories)
cac_by_channel_b2b.cac_basis: Partner recruitment and enablement time, plus the cost of the certifications required to qualify.
cac_by_channel_b2b.scale_ceiling: BLOCKED, not low. Published MSP vendor-selection criteria require SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, current penetration-test reports, SSO and MFA, audit logging, partner training material and pre- and post-sales support. SOC 2 Type II alone is a six-to-twelve-month process with real cost and is unreachable on a sub-$100/month budget. This channel is not expensive; it is closed.

cac_by_channel_b2b.channel: Launch moment (Product Hunt, Hacker News Show HN, MSP trade press)
cac_by_channel_b2b.cac_basis: One-time cohort, not a recurring channel. Modelled as a fixed spike of 20-60 signups producing a handful of paying customers.
cac_by_channel_b2b.scale_ceiling: ONE-TIME. Model it as a cohort of 20-60 signups, not as acquisition. The audience on those platforms skews to developers rather than MSP owners, so relevance is poor.

skipped_channels: Paid LinkedIn: excluded by the bootstrap budget filter. Would need $600-1,500 CAC against a $100/month total budget, so it cannot be tested, let alone scaled.
Paid Google search: excluded by the same filter. Category CPCs are bid up by funded security vendors.
ASO, TikTok organic, paid social, influencer: not applicable to the B2B lane.

Warm network: excluded because it does not exist. The founder's inner circle contains an AI automation agency owner, not an MSP. This is the decisive difference from the agency-facing ideas in this project, where the warm network was the strongest channel.
viable_channels: MSP peer groups and operator communities
recommended_first_channel: MSP peer groups and operator communities, with comparison content started in parallel from week one so it is ramping before community participation exhausts.
recommended_first_channel_rationale: It is the only channel that clears 3:1 in both the base and pessimistic cases, has a payback of two months, and does not require money the founder does not have or certifications the founder cannot obtain. It is also the weakest recommendation this project has produced, because the ceiling is 10-25 customers and the community in question bans vendors who participate the way a founder needs to participate. Content is started alongside it not because it is good but because it is the only channel with a ceiling above a few dozen, and it needs a year to ramp at 15 hours a week.

conservative_12mo.assumption: Community participation only, no content traction inside the first year, one launch cohort.

base_12mo.assumption: Community plus a launch cohort plus the first content-driven signups in months 9-12. Matches the market_size.json year-1 SOM of roughly $33,600 ARR.

optimistic_24mo.assumption: Content compounds through year two and the churn base case holds. Requires that no MSP-platform incumbent ships a competing module in that window, which the competitive analysis rates as unlikely.

market_insights_adjustments: trend_velocity rising-fast would normally lower organic CAC as category search demand grows; here it is offset because the same growth attracted six vendors publishing comparison content for the same queries. Content CAC is adjusted up rather than down.

The MSP channel's documented per-endpoint resale motion (Control D at $2/endpoint, DNSFilter MSP from $150/month) supports the pricing but not the acquisition: those vendors reached MSPs through partner programmes this founder cannot build.

Community activity is real and identifiable (r/msp, MSP peer groups, ChannelE2E readership), which is why the community channel is costed at the low end of the B2B band despite its hostility to vendors.
viability_verdict_rationale: By the rubric this is viable: two channels clear 3:1 in the base case and one of them is organic. The ratios are genuine and the payback on the recommended channel is two months, so a customer acquired here pays for itself quickly. The verdict is recorded as the rubric computes it, and the caveats below carry what the ratio cannot see. Note explicitly for the reader: this file says the unit economics work, not that the customers are reachable. Channel accessibility is scored in distribution.json, and that is where this idea's actual problem is measured.
blended_ceiling_basis: Sum of the realistic ceilings of the channels classified viable or marginal, excluding the one-time launch cohort and contributing zero for the partner channel, which is blocked by SOC 2 Type II rather than merely limited. MSP peer communities contribute the midpoint of their 10-25 range, roughly 18; content SEO and outbound contribute about 12 more within a realistic 24-month horizon at 15 hours a week. At the $199 primary tier, 30 customers is roughly $72,000 ARR, which is the practical ceiling of this business as currently routed.
critical_caveats: The viability verdict measures ratio, not ceiling. The two channels that clear 3:1 have combined realistic ceilings of roughly 25-35 customers, which is about $70,000-85,000 ARR. Good unit economics on a business that cannot grow past a ceiling is a lifestyle outcome at best, and this ceiling arrives below the point where the founder could hire help to raise it.

The single most consequential input is one the founder cannot change: whether Microsoft's Purview coverage improves faster than this product's differentiation. Every LTV case assumes the separate invoice survives the renewal conversation.

The partner channel is closed rather than expensive. SOC 2 Type II is a documented selection criterion for MSP security vendors and is unreachable at a sub-$100/month budget. Any plan that routes through MSP partner programmes should be treated as requiring capital this founder has said he does not have.

The warm-network advantage that made the agency-facing ideas in this project attractive does not exist here. The founder's inner circle is an AI automation agency, not an MSP, and the two channels do not overlap.

Churn between 4% and 10% swings contribution LTV by 2.5x and flips the content channel between 3.0:1 and 1.8:1. Measuring real churn is the highest-value data collection in year one, and it cannot begin until customers exist.
